reviews.title: excellent performance and combination
reviews.comment: Initially, I had some problems only with the software, but Lian Li's support promptly helped me and now everything works perfectly. Without a doubt, it was one of the best AIOs I've ever had, super clean, quiet, excellent appearance, installation was super easy, the software configuration is very good, it has good quality and bright colors, and many options. My motherboard is a Gigabyte LGA 1851 Z890 Aorus Master and everything is synchronized with the Gigabyte software. Excellent cooler, I very recommend!
reviews.author: RMK2025

reviews.title: The Software is easy to use!
reviews.comment: Installing was straight forward and easy on my AMD chipset. I found the software easy to use and making custom videos was a breeze. The performance is really good. MY temps stay below 60c. I am using triple fans on top and bottom as an experiment. The airflow must be good staying at those temps. Noise is minimal from the pump but you can tell well the fans are runing lol. I honestly dont even notice the fan noise. The color matches my case and most of the components for a clean look. I definitely think its worth the price.
reviews.author: john with a jeep

reviews.title: Quiet, Cool, and Pretty
reviews.comment: Off rip, I'll admit that I definitely prefer the actual colors/RGB of Corsair, having owned some of their products in the past. That being said, I don't know if there's a cooler that looks better for the performance and cost of this unit. I was very worried about heat going into my new build, since I got an i9 14900k for cheap. So far after installation, I have had absolutely no issues with thermals. The highest I saw it go was 80c on the first day of use, and since then it's been stuck between 50-65C depending on the game I'm playing. I have yet to use it for any serious media application yet, but I will update when I end up seeing how that performs. So far though, it keeps the CPU cool, looks nice, and is pretty customizable. I was on a NZXT x62 before with an i9 10850k, and it could not really handle anything higher than 1.35v without hitting 90C+. Obviously this is a 3 fan rad so it's bound to do better, but I am still very impressed with what I've seen. It was also the easiest AIO I have ever installed, and daisy chains easily to other fans if you'd like to do an all INF-fan build. Overall really solid. I will update if I end up having the notorious pump failure issue, but so far it's great.
reviews.author: Matteo D'Angelo

reviews.title: Biggest waste of money in my current build
reviews.comment: I generally don't write reviews, but this thing has been such a thorn in my side. First of all, when you first turn your computer on you'll notice that the pump is extremely loud at default settings. Like hearing it down the hallway loud. I waited a week to see if the bubbles would settle and make it quiet like people say it is, tilted my PC to work them out, and no change. So I figured maybe I had a dud and returned it to swap them out. Same story. I asked their support about it, gave videos, showed the audio spectrum near the PC at different pump speeds, and was told this is normal. I had to lower the pump speed from the what is already mid-range 2300rpm default to specifically 1690rpm as both 1700rpm and 1680rpm have higher noise. Then there's the software. It's terrible. For months it didn't even work properly and you had to regularly reinstall it to reset and have it working again for another couple of weeks until it tried to do an update and crashed itself. And the service running in the background is constantly polling the hardware for information like power usage, temperatures, etc. Which makes sense for something like this, but it was causing issues for me in SteamVR and some games with stuttering until I killed the process. And it's a dice roll every time there's an update whether it will start using up 10% of your CPU constantly; increasing the temperatures and eating up resources. This is on a 14900k, mind you. But the LCD has its own issues: the one of the big things that made me want to pay $275 for this on launch. It works great for about 6 months, but then you'll notice once in a while the image flickers. Then it happens more and more frequently. You try to change images or background colors to see if it fixes it and notice the previous images are "sticking" like there is screen burn in or something, but it very slowly resolves itself over time if you're lucky. Then it really looks like there is screen burn in when you have nothing but a white background on that LCD and the whole thing looks like someone held a candle to it. This has happened to me with the original LCD that came with it AND the replacement they sent me 8 months ago. Which, by the way, they won't just replace the cooler. They'll send you a new LCD and have you rip apart your cooler to put the LCD on. So, if you're not prepared to do that, be ready to ask someone for help. Pros: - Cools a 14900k decently well considering how much heat that puts out. - Infinity fans look nice and are pretty quiet when not cranked up really high. - LCD looks nice when it works and there is a simple editor to put videos and gifs in it. Cons: - LCD has a life span of 6-8 months and has needed replacement twice. - Loud unless you lower the pump speed a lot and find the magic number to make it silent. - Troublesome RMA process that some people won't be comfortable with. - The supporting software is terrible and either causes issues or eats up too much system resources for what it does. Not worth it. I gave it 1 star since it did a decent job of cooling, especially for running at only 1690rpm and being attached to a 14900k. Maybe just get the non-LCD version if noise doesn't bother you and use third party software or motherboard controls, because I'm not sure they have a QA process or proper testing procedures.
reviews.author: Zoey

reviews.title: Blending Elite Cooling with Dynamic Visuals
reviews.comment: Cooling Performance Beyond the dazzling display, the core function of an AIO is cooling, and Lian Li's 360mm LCD coolers consistently deliver top-tier performance. Powerful Pump: These AIOs typically feature an Asetek 8th generation pump, known for its high efficiency and quiet operation. With pump speeds reaching up to 3600 RPM (or even 3200-4200 RPM depending on the model), it ensures robust coolant flow for effective heat transfer from the CPU. Effective Radiator Design: The 360mm aluminum radiator, with its optimized fin design, provides a large surface area for heat dissipation. When paired with the included high static pressure fans, it efficiently expels heat from even the most demanding CPUs. Thermal Performance: In real-world scenarios and benchmarks, these coolers consistently keep high-TDP processors (like Intel i9s and AMD Ryzen 9s, including X3D variants) well within safe operating temperatures, even under sustained heavy loads like gaming or video rendering. Users often report CPU temperatures well below critical thresholds, even in demanding applications like Cinebench. Low Noise Profile: Despite their cooling prowess, the combination of efficient FDB fans and a well-designed pump means these AIOs can maintain a surprisingly low noise profile, especially at idle or moderate loads. The fans offer a wide RPM range, allowing for tuning between silence and maximum performance via software. LCD Screen & Customization This is the feature that truly sets the Lian Li LCD AIO apart. The integrated IPS LCD screen is not a gimmick; it's a powerful customization tool: Vibrant Display: The 2.88-inch screen is bright (up to 500 nits) and offers sharp resolution, making displayed content clearly visible. Real-time Monitoring: Through Lian Li's L-Connect 3 software, users can display a wealth of real-time system information, including CPU/GPU temperatures, load, frequencies, fan speeds, and more. The layouts are customizable, allowing users to prioritize the data most important to them. Personalization: Beyond system stats, the screen supports custom images, GIFs, and even short videos. This allows for unparalleled personalization, transforming the CPU block into a dynamic visual centerpiece that can match your build's theme or express your personality. Software Integration (L-Connect 3): The L-Connect 3 software is the command center for the cooler, offering intuitive control over pump speed, fan curves, and extensive customization options for the LCD screen and ARGB lighting. While software can sometimes be a point of contention for PC components, L-Connect 3 generally provides a comprehensive and user-friendly experience, though occasional software glitches have been reported (and often addressed by updates). Installation & Compatibility Installation is generally straightforward for a 360mm AIO. Lian Li includes mounting hardware for all modern CPU sockets (Intel LGA 1700/1851, AMD AM4/AM5), ensuring wide compatibility. The pre-installed fans (on some models) and thoughtful cable management options (including daisy-chainable ARGB fans for less cable clutter) further simplify the process. The flexible tubing and rotatable pump block make it adaptable to various case layouts. Areas for Improvement Price Point: As a premium product with an integrated LCD screen and top-tier cooling performance, the Lian Li LCD 360mm AIO comes with a higher price tag compared to non-LCD or less feature-rich AIOs. It's an investment in both performance and aesthetics. Software Dependency: While L-Connect 3 is powerful, reliance on software for full customization means some users might encounter occasional software-related quirks or a learning curve. Pump Noise (Specific Batches): While generally quiet, some early batches of certain models experienced pump rattling or whining at specific RPM ranges. Lian Li has actively addressed these issues with revised designs and firmware updates, but it's worth checking user reviews for the specific model and batch if concern arises. Tube Orientation (Hydroshift): For the Hydroshift series, optimal performance is achieved when the tubes on the pump are oriented upwards, which might dictate placement in some builds. Conclusion The Lian Li LCD 360mm AIO cooler is an exceptional cooling solution that masterfully blends high-performance thermal management with stunning visual customization. It delivers powerful and efficient cooling for even the hottest CPUs, while its vibrant, customizable LCD screen transforms the humble CPU block into a dynamic display of system data or personal flair. While it represents a premium investment and requires software management, for enthusiasts building a high-end system where both top-tier performance and eye-catching aesthetics are paramount, the Lian Li LCD 360mm AIO is a highly recommended and truly insightful choice.
